post.description: collection is totals. The body is NDJSON (Content-Type application/x-ndjson), not JSON: one day per line, { "day": "YYYY-MM-DD", "part": 0, "totals": { "<metric>": { "<key>": { "c": <count>, "s": <sum> } } } }, the day in your business time zone and the keys as readable text; at most 1,000 lines or 4 MB. Each metric must be one Growth counts, with keys of the form it writes, a whole count of 0 or more and a finite sum (only revenue, duration, vital_value and vital_page keep sums); unknown fields are refused by name. A day replaces the day's document, so totals counted live that day are replaced too. Nothing is sent and no raw events are made. 404 not_found for another collection; 415 unsupported_media_type without NDJSON.

post.description: One rule per line with the columns from, match, to, code and note in any order (any letter case; Redirect from and source are read as from, Redirect to and destination as to, status as code; other columns are ignored), separated by commas, semicolons or tabs (the header line's). A from that has a rule changes it; the others are created; nothing is deleted. Each line is checked as on create; a from twice in the file, more than 5,000 rules in all, and loops and chains are problems. A dry run (the default) changes nothing and lists every change and problem; a real import with problems answers 422 validation_failed (errors at /csv/<line>/<column>) and imports nothing. At most 5,000 lines and 4 MB. Written to the activity log. The admin twin needs the redirects.edit permission.

get.summary: The robots.txt your site serves
get.description: Answers text/plain, not JSON: serve it as https://<your domain>/robots.txt. Your rules (control characters and their own Sitemap lines left out) with the presets' Disallow lines in each group, right after its User-agent lines (a User-agent: * group of them first when your rules have none): search results (the search parameters of Searches and 404s), sort and filter parameters and private pages, as set; then with 'Block AI training crawlers' a group keeping those crawlers off the whole site, then a Sitemap line per sitemap address on your domain (at most 50; none set: /sitemap.xml).

post.description: Reads your site now and checks it: robots.txt, the sitemap it names (else /sitemap.xml; for an index, its first 3 files), the pages, an address that does not exist (it must answer 404 or 410) and the old paths of up to 3 of your redirect rules; with Web Vitals and Searches and 404s on, also your visitors' Web Vitals of the last 28 days and the 404 log of the last 90 days. A full run (no paths) adds sample pages from the sitemap (a product, a category, a landing or listing page and a glossary page, when your site has them) and is kept: asked again within 5 minutes, it answers the kept report (cached: true) without reading your site. Reads are made a few at a time, each at most 8 seconds and 2 MB (a sitemap file 16 MB), the whole run at most 25 seconds; redirects are not followed. Needs the database (the report is kept there). 422 validation_failed when paths is not a list of at most 20. 10 calls an hour per website.

action.description: What was done, for example payment.refunded.

target.description: The id of what it was done to.

label.description: A name for the target, for example an order number.

Actor.description: Who did it: user (the acting user of a server call), staff (a ticket's user) or server.

CollectEvent.description: One event as the page script sends it. Members that do not belong to the type are ignored; an event without a known type or a path is dropped.

path.description: The page's path from / (not //); the query string and fragment are cut off; at most 300 characters, no spaces.

visit.description: page_view: true when it starts a visit (no page view in the last 30 minutes in this tab).

device.description: page_view: the device class from the screen width (another value counts as desktop).

referrer.description: page_view: the referring host (a host other than your domain becomes the source). not_found with the sessions detail: where the visitor came from (a path on your website or another site's host).

campaign.description: page_view: the visit's campaign (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign); a source replaces the referrer as the source.

source.description: Kept in lower case, at most 100 characters.

medium.description: Kept in lower case, at most 100 characters.

items.description: view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, purchase: the items (the first 50 are kept; one without an id is dropped).

id.description: The product id (at most 80 characters kept).

variantId.description: The variant id (at most 80 characters kept).

quantity.description: 1 when missing or out of range.

value.description: Funnel events: the amount in minor units, a whole number 0–1,000,000,000,000 (kept only with currency, else 0). vital: the measurement in milliseconds (CLS × 1000), 0–600,000, rounded.

currency.description: Funnel events: ISO 4217 code of value.

orderId.description: purchase: your order number (at most 80 characters kept).

term.description: search: what was searched for (kept in lower case with spaces collapsed, at most 100 characters; an empty term drops the event).

results.description: search: how many results it found (0 also counts it as an empty search).

session.description: With the sessions detail: the tab's random session id (another value: no session facts are kept).

browser.description: With a session: the browser family (another value is kept as null).

os.description: With a session: the system family (another value is kept as null).

page.description: page_view with a session: which page of the session it is (2 makes the session engaged).

gap.description: page_view with a session: milliseconds since the session's last page view (adds to its duration).

Connection.description: A connection as screens see it: secrets never come back.

last4.description: The last 4 characters of the secret ('' when none).

Count.description: How many records match the list's filters.

capped.description: True when there are more than 100,000 (count is then 100,000).

Counts.description: The matching records counted by one field.

groups.description: Value → count, the 50 largest groups; a missing value is counted as none.

Event.description: One recorded event (anonymous: never an IP address, user agent, cookie or cross-site id). Removed at expiresAt by the database's expiry index.

path.description: The page's path (never the query string).

at.description: When it was recorded (events of one batch are a millisecond apart, in the order sent).

expiresAt.description: When it is removed: the retention set when it was recorded.

data.description: What else is kept, by type.

session.description: With the sessions detail: the tab's random session id. Absent without it.

browser.description: With a session: the browser family.

os.description: With a session: the system family.

city.description: With a session and Record country on: the city your host's request header gave.

EventPage.description: One page of recorded events, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as cursor for the next page (null: the last page).

EventType.description: page_view: Visitor analytics; view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, purchase: Conversion funnel; search, not_found: Searches and 404s; vital: Web Vitals.

locale.description: A language tag such as en-US or fr-FR, or '' for the viewer's (en-US in text the server makes).

status.description: What IndexNow answered (202: received, the key is checked later).

Journey.description: One session of the range with its first steps (the event log has them all).

session.description: Pass it as session to GET /v1/events for every event of the visit.

duration.description: Seconds from its first to its last event.

device.description: From the visit's first page view (null when the range does not hold it).

country.description: Two letters, or (unknown); from the visit's first page view.

source.description: A host, a campaign source or (direct); from the visit's first page view.

steps.description: The first 30 events in order, Web Vitals left out.

value.description: Funnel events with a currency: minor units.

NotFoundData.description: not_found: nothing more; with the sessions detail where the visitor came from.

from.description: A path on your website or another site's host; null when unknown.

Notice.description: The notice bar while it shows.

linkUrl.description: An https address or a path on your website; null when the setting is neither.

PageViewData.description: page_view. A visit's first page also keeps where the visit came from, the device and the country.

source.description: A visit's first page: the campaign source, the referring host, or (direct).

medium.description: A visit's first page: the campaign medium ('' without one).

campaign.description: A visit's first page: the campaign name ('' without one).

country.description: A visit's first page: two letters from your host's request header, or (unknown).

page.description: With a session: which page of the session it is.

Problem.description: An error (RFC 9457, application/problem+json). The last segment of type is a stable code, for example validation_failed.

requestId.description: Quote it when you contact support.

errors.description: validation_failed: what is wrong, field by field.

path.description: JSON Pointer of the field, for example /amount.

from.description: The old path, normalized: one leading slash, repeated slashes as one, . and .. resolved, letters in one Unicode form (NFC), characters outside URLs percent-encoded (upper-case hex), no trailing slash except for /, letter case kept.

match.description: exact: the path itself; prefix: the path and every path under it, segment by segment (/blog matches /blog and /blog/news, not /blogger), keeping the rest of the path (/blog → /news sends /blog/a to /news/a). An exact rule wins, else the longest prefix.

to.description: The new page: a path on your website (with its own query string and fragment if any) or an https address on another site; null for 410.

code.description: 301 or 308: moved for good (308 keeps the request method, for forms); 410: gone for good (no to).

note.description: Your own words about the rule.

RedirectChanges.description: The members of a rule to change; they are merged into the stored rule and the whole is checked as on create. A code changed to 410 without to drops the stored to.

from.description: The old path from /, or an address on your website's domain (or its www. twin), read as its path; without ? or # (rules match the path only); at most 1,000 characters once normalized.

match.description: exact: the path itself; prefix: the path and every path under it, segment by segment (/blog matches /blog and /blog/news, not /blogger), keeping the rest of the path (/blog → /news sends /blog/a to /news/a). An exact rule wins, else the longest prefix.

to.description: The new page: a path from / (a query string and fragment are kept) or an https address (an https address on your own domain is kept as its path); leave it out or null for 410; at most 2,048 characters once normalized.

code.description: 301 or 308: moved for good (308 keeps the request method, for forms); 410: gone for good (no to).

RedirectImport.description: What a CSV import did, or would do (a dry run).

rows.description: Lines of the file without the header.

unchanged.description: Lines already as the stored rule.

changes.description: Every rule made or changed (to be, in a dry run), in file order; lines with a problem are left out.

before.description: update: the stored rule's match, to, code and note.

errors.description: Every problem found (a real import with problems answers 422 and imports nothing).

RedirectInput.description: A new redirect rule. Unknown members are refused by name.

RedirectList.description: Every rule of the website, A to Z by from, for edge middleware.

version.description: Changes whenever a rule changes; the ETag is it in quotes.

code.description: 301 or 308: moved for good (308 keeps the request method, for forms); 410: gone for good (no to).

RedirectMatch.description: The rule that answers an address, and where to send the visitor.

match.description: exact: the path itself; prefix: the path and every path under it, segment by segment (/blog matches /blog and /blog/news, not /blogger), keeping the rest of the path (/blog → /news sends /blog/a to /news/a). An exact rule wins, else the longest prefix.

code.description: 301 or 308: moved for good (308 keeps the request method, for forms); 410: gone for good (no to).

location.description: Send it as the Location header with code: the new page, with the rest of a prefix rule's path and the visitor's query string added after the target's own (/old?utm_source=x → /new?ref=a&utm_source=x); a path on your website or an https address. null for 410: answer 410 Gone.

RedirectPage.description: One page of redirect rules, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as cursor for the next page (null: the last page).

RedirectRowProblem.description: A problem of one line of a CSV file.

line.description: The line of the file (1 is the header; also used for the whole file).

path.description: The column as a JSON pointer (/from, /match, /to, /code, /note), '' for the whole file.

code.description: Why, for your own words: from or to required (empty), not_path, other_host, query (from has ? or #), too_long, twice (the from is on an earlier line), not_match, not_code, not_target, not_https, gone (a 410 rule with a to), not_text, loop, chain and removed (the rule's target is removed by a 410 rule); for the whole file empty, unterminated_quote, too_many_rows, columns (no from column) and too_many (more than 5,000 rules in all).

steps.description: loop, chain, removed: the addresses one request would pass (/… stands for any path under a prefix).

RedirectSuggestions.description: Rules to add, from the 404 log.

from.description: The first day read (business time zone).

recording.description: Whether Searches and 404s records 404s now (with it off, only older days have any).

path.description: A missing page no rule answers (normalized).

hits.description: Times visitors reached it in those days.

to.description: A page visitors did open with the same last segment (the most viewed), else null.

Report.description: The analytics of a range of days, from the daily totals. Parts of a feature that is off, and the session parts without the sessions detail, are null.

timeZone.description: The zone of the days: business.json timeZone, else UTC.

days.description: Every day of the range, in order.

detail.description: The Detail setting of Visitor analytics.

pages.description: Page views by path, most first.

sources.description: Visits by source (a host, a campaign source or (direct)), most first.

devices.description: Visits by device class (mobile, tablet, desktop), most first.

countries.description: Visits by country (two letters, or (unknown)), most first.

averageDuration.description: Seconds from a session's first to its last page (null without sessions).

browsers.description: Sessions detail only: sessions by browser family, most first.

systems.description: Sessions detail only: sessions by system family, most first.

cities.description: Sessions detail only: sessions by city (for example Lyon, FR), most first.

live.description: Sessions detail only: sessions with an event in the last 5 minutes, judged when you ask.

pages.description: The page each live session last viewed, most first.

journeys.description: Sessions detail only: the 20 latest sessions of the range, newest first.

value.description: Minor units (a whole number unless an import brought fractions).

searches.description: Searches and 404s only: site searches by term, most first.

emptySearches.description: Searches and 404s only: searches that found nothing, by term.

notFound.description: Searches and 404s only: missing pages by path.

notFoundFrom.description: Sessions detail and Searches and 404s only: each missing page and where its visitors came from, most first.

from.description: A path on your website, another site's host, or (direct).

vitalPages.description: Sessions detail and Web Vitals only: each page's averages, the slowest largest paint first.

samples.description: Measurements of every vital on the page.

averages.description: Milliseconds (CLS × 1000); null for a vital not measured there.

vitals.description: Web Vitals only: each vital, in the order LCP, INP, CLS, FCP, TTFB.

SeoCheck.description: One check, with its title, the reason (what was found) and the fix steps from your widget texts (Settings → Texts: seo.check.<id>.title, seo.check.<id>.<finding> and seo.check.<id>.fix).

id.description: robots_txt to web_vitals_site check the whole site; the others each page (site_data on the home page; product_data, price_match and server_html on product pages; breadcrumbs on product, category and listing pages; web_vitals with the sessions detail).

status.description: warn: to improve; fail: to fix.

finding.description: What was found, a stable code per check (ok when it passed; for example missing, several, not_self, blocked, soft, not_shown). The docs list them.

page.description: The address read (robots.txt, the sitemap, the address that does not exist, or the page); null for checks of several addresses.

status.description: reachable, robots_txt, sitemap, sitemap_urls, soft_404, redirects_live: the HTTP status it answered (0: no answer).

ms.description: reachable, response_time: how long the page took to answer our read, in milliseconds.

length.description: title, description: its length in characters.

count.description: How many: h1 headings, images without alt text or size, JSON-LD blocks (structured_data: the broken ones when invalid), canonical links (several), verification tags, Sitemap lines, addresses (robots_blocks, sitemap, sitemap_urls, redirect_suggestions), redirect rules (redirects_live).

location.description: A redirect's Location header (reachable, robots_txt, soft_404).

path.description: The first address concerned, as a path: blocked (robots_blocks), not answering 200 (sitemap_urls, sitemap's file_missing), a rule not applied (redirects_live), the most visited missing address (redirect_suggestions).

url.description: canonical: the canonical link as written; sitemap_urls: an address of another site.

rule.description: robots_blocks: the rule that blocks it, as written (Disallow: /cart).

missing.description: product_data, site_data: what the structured data lacks, comma-separated.

price.description: price_match: the price of the structured data (1250.00).

hits.description: redirect_suggestions: visits to the most visited missing address.

expected.description: redirects_live: the code the rule answers.

pattern.description: web_vitals: the pages it is measured on (/products/*: every page at that level).

samples.description: web_vitals, web_vitals_site: how many measurements it is judged on.

vital.description: web_vitals, web_vitals_site: the vital to work on (LCP, INP or CLS).

value.description: web_vitals: that vital's average (2.6 s, 250 ms, 0.12).

good.description: web_vitals_site: the share of the visits measured with a good value of that vital, in percent.

fix.description: The steps to fix it ('' when it passed).

test.description: Google's Rich Results Test of the page (checks of a page; null for the site's).

kind.description: From its address (home) and its structured data: Product or ProductGroup (product), DefinedTerm (glossary), CollectionPage or ItemList (category; with a query string, listing: a landing or listing page), else page.

sampled.description: true: picked from your sitemap; false: the home page, a page of the checklist's settings or a path you sent.

SeoReport.description: The SEO checklist: the whole site's checks, then each page's.

cached.description: true: the kept report of an earlier full run (GET …/report, or a full run asked within 5 minutes of it); nothing was read now.

checks.description: The site's checks, then each page's (a check that cannot be judged is left out: robots.txt that does not answer, no Web Vitals measured).

pages.description: The pages read: the home page, the checklist's pages (or the paths you sent), then the sample pages from your sitemap (a full run).

colors.description: Color name → #rrggbb (the product's CSS supplies the others).

TotalsKey.description: The key of an imported day.

ValueSource.description: Where a value comes from: saved for this website, the global default, or built in.
